en: Having bowed to the Lord of Śrī, the bestower of desired fruits upon those who prostrate, this concise *Śamāna-śikṣā* is composed for the easy understanding of the followers of the Ṛgveda.
A *visarjanīya* preceded by the vowel *ā* and followed by a voiced consonant (*ghoṣavat*) is elided when it comes into contact with a consonant (*vyañjana*) followed by *ś*,
*s*, or *s*; I shall now declare those words according to the sequence of phonemes in these rules of euphonic combination (*saṃhitā*).

In this context, *iṅgya* is a separate word, as is the state of being a cause (*nimittatva*), and there is a plurality of words among the *iṅgyas*. The preceding portion, however, is the *avagraha*. That which is taken as the cause is precisely what constitutes a "word" (*pada*) in this definition.
Excluding the first and second [classes], the three classes [of each] beginning with the semivowels (*antasthā*) and the letter *ha* are proclaimed to be voiced (*ghoṣavat*).
Thus has the definition of the "similar" (*samāna*) been stated in brief.

The three classes beginning with *ga*, *ja*, and *ḍa*; the consonants beginning with *da* and *ba*; those from *ya* to *va*; the letter *ha*; and the letters *śa* and *sa* when not joined with another—this is the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*).

Unpleasing, you did not yield to her; windless, unattaining, water-winning, you saw no enemies; unseen, you went on paths that were not seen; you propped up the clouds of another; unfrowning, you filled the waters; you placed songs within the cow; unharmed, uninjured, unscathed, at home, not stingy, spotless, foremost, watery, unassailable, most internal, without heroes, unequalled, unknown, without a guardian, sinless, free from disease, terminal, blameless, faceless, you have warded off misfortune; unborn, not lowland, of the future, neighing, Aṅgiras-like, flowerless, chariotless, unassailable, boneless, udderless, Apsaras-like.

You were born for him whose followers stood firm, surpassing others in their speed; the red, unmeasured, and unwearied ones flew down. Your flawless, united, and steadfast paths lead around the dwelling; O immortal ones, you are the red power, whose purpose is the ocean. The diseases have been driven away and made distinct; the immortals have gone forth from afar, like beloved kinsmen. The ancient ones, with their horses, have brought glory through their songs; they are beyond the winds and the floods, like wise and ageless ones who, being blameless, send forth their power—the seventy-one verses. The two swift-moving ones, striving together, have come to the Aryas; the Ādityas have performed what was not done before and have attained their goals. They brandish their ancient weapons; six verses.

Desiring, kindled by others, offered, vigorous, difficult to seize, sent forth from afar, the heroes—the grains—having abandoned the clans of Rudra and Bṛhaspati, go toward the singer. Those songs of yours which the woman, seeking strength, offers like all the cows—strike down these former ones and the nine.
3. Moving forward, fleeing, the lords—three. 4.

Dawn, the ruddy one, swelling in the cauldron, grown fat in the wide expanse, rising up for the drinking; let them reach us even as they are fierce. They take heed of the nights; these are the bright ones. 5.
*Ūmā*, *ūtā*, *ūrṇā*, *ūrdhvā*; *nadyaḥ* becomes *paraścatvāri*.
(6) *Ṛkṣā*, *ṛbhukṣā*, *ṛṣvā*, *ṛjrā*; *vātaparaścatvāri*.
(7) *Ekasyā evāḥ*, *kṣamyaham*, *iyam*, *etā*, *vinanipaḥ*; *paraśca enāḥ*, *anantodāttaścatvāri*. (8)
*ojā okā dve* (9);

*aibhirjaganvān*, *dyauriva saṃvatsaram*, *gomāyuḥ*, *atyāḥ*, *sūryasyeva*, *suṣvāṇāsaḥ*, *vimṛjyamānaḥ*, *krāṇā rudrāḥ*, *upabrahmāṇi*, *eteṣu sarvatra nātvānamasau*; *ṛṣātrāvagrahaśca nityam*, excluding *na vyāsthāḥ*; *sthustha bhavantu paraḥ sarvatra* (10).

The rays, the playful ones, the banners, the channels, the youths, the maidens—those with braided hair on the right side of the quarters; their whips are Soma, made into a steed; the quarters, truth, and security, establishing them; the descendants of Kaṇva, desires, the waters, the ancient ones, the dwellings, the laws, the kṣatriyas—seventeen groups (11).

The Gotamas, the embryos, the villages, the seizers, the praised ones, the divine wives, the cows, the seized ones, the deep ones, our secret ones, the cows, not preceded by "bad," the protector, the pair—you two shall be; the months, the gods, beyond, being praised for glory, the god-beyond—fourteen (12). The driving away, the terrible ones—one (13).
Candramas, cetā, cakṣās, cakrāṇa, cakṣāṇā, in the thought (matī) caniṣṭhā, citrā, ārodhasvatī, yāmebhis, paras, aśvāpa, candrā, riśādasaḥ, paras, ca, cakramāṇā, rihanti, paras, nava 14;
chinnā, ekā 15;

juṣṭā, joṣā, juguryā, jñeyā, jajñānā, jyāyā, juhvānā, jīvā, jyā, jehamānā, jñā, jihvāyā, jā, johuvānā, indrajyeṣṭhā, agninā, sujihvā, janā, na, dyāpūrvaḥ, marutaḥ, yugā, gobhis, devebhyas, mahinā, paras, jātā, juṣāṇā, yūyam, paras, ekonaviṃśatiḥ 16.

The drops, the householders, the given, the ordained, the lowly, the milked, the wondrous, the fierce, the burnt, the gifts, the dūrvā-grass at the journey, and those who bestow—these you have not hidden away; nor are they beyond the reach of strength, since even the firm mountains and the Dāsas, though wearying themselves, become visible in the evening. May the calamity depart; milking the clarified butter, the divine invocation is like a cow that yields all things for the one who has been born. Beyond his skill is nothing, beyond him in heaven is nothing, beyond him in newness is nothing, beyond him in giving is nothing, and beyond him in meditation is nothing; he whose [powers] are invincible from of old.

*Paraḥ*, *devāḥ*, *nobhā*, *pūrvaḥ*, *eṣaḥ*, *uṣāḥ*, *aśvinā*, *vartiḥ*, *tāvām*, *indrāparvatā*, *pra vaḥ*, *mitrāya*, *kūṣṭhaḥ*, *pra nu*, *yam*, *yuvaṃ*, *imāḥ*, *uvām*, *mahe*, *śulkāya*, *uti antāḥ*, *vān*, *dasrā*, *hi*, *indra*, *somam*, *eteṣu*, *devāḥ*, *na*, *aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ*. (18) *Dhṛṣitāḥ*, *dhārāvarāḥ*, *dhīrāḥ*, *dhāyāḥ*, *na*, *dhenāḥ*, *dhāḥ*, *anapapūrvaḥ*, *dhānāḥ*, *na*, *vipūrvaḥ*, *dhārāḥ*, *na*, *pracyutaḥ*, *pūrvaḥ*, *dhiṣṇyāḥ*, *ye*, *paraḥ*, *nava*.
(19) *Navyāḥ*, *navedāḥ*, *nidāyāḥ*, *nīlāḥ*, *nagnāḥ*, *unnītāḥ*, *sunīthāḥ*, *hastena*, *aryāḥ*, *navāḥ*, *naḥ*, *paraḥ*, *nava*. (20)

The winged ones, the rain-clouds, the progeny, the fillers, the sinners, the paths, the purifiers, the dappled ones, the armies, the mountains, the splendors, those who cross over, the journeys, the springs, the flowing ones, the offspring of Pajrā, the swelling ones, the purified ones, the ornaments, the dangling ones, those born of the highest, the impelled, the instructed, the covered ones, the wives, the most desirable among riches, the dear ones—Indra’s feet have stepped upon them; we would fain be dear to Indra through the Soma-pressings, for the first ones indeed spoke thus.

The swelling cows have gone along the paths between the two worlds (heaven and earth). O sons, may you not be thirsty; the plants have a hundred purifiers. Those that are on earth and those beyond, which do not shed blood—go forth among these friends. "Of this earth, no one..."—among these [verses] ending with *mevātasya*. "The leaves, the honeyed speech..."—one less than forty (thirty-nine). 21. "The ploughshares, one. 22.
"The sacrificial grass, the Brahmins, the awakened, the waking, the pressing, the terrifying"—six. 23.
Bhikṣamāṇā, Bhāmā, Bharā, Bharatā, Bhindānā, Bhramā, Bhojā, Bṛhadbhā, Bhṛtā—those among whom you are supreme; since we have stepped forth and awakened to these, may there be ten auspicious ones. 24.

The foolish, the wise, the wild beasts, the gentle, the rejoicing, the intoxicated, the mild, the mortals being purified, the friends, the youths, the deaths, the exhilarated, the thinking—your longings, O Vadhryamati, are like those of men; the months with their wealth of cattle, the pure ones, the thoughts, measuring out wisdom, they bear it as human beings; the Maruts, rejoicing, like the spokes of a wheel, moving beyond the mind, like human generations; beyond illusion, not by illusion, the first—twenty-six. 25.

The worshipful ones, striving, sacrificing, yoked together, worthy of sacrifice, warriors, to be sought, those who must be approached—the wasting diseases with their brilliant courses mount up; the sacrifices, immovable at their end, are joined when they have gone beyond. Yoked like a mother on her chariot, the bearer has gone far away for the sake of dominion. Rise up, O you of the golden ornament! Having abandoned us, the protectors and the sacrificial gifts depart; this Agni shall become our [protector]. O Vāyu, the bright one shines as of old; Agni has come to the cows, beautiful to behold. Those with excellent dominion—will you not drink of this pressed juice? These [songs] are for you both, along with the thunderbolt.
The Gharma hymn consists of sixteen verses: *samantām*, *ayo bhūḥ*, *abhīvartena*, *pra nūnam*, *eteṣu*, *yāḥ*, *prameya*, *indrāgnī*, *etayoḥ*, and the second [verse] of *ṛṇapūrvaḥ*.

(26) The Reṣaṇā hymn consists of sixteen verses: *reṣaṇā*, *retāḥ*, *rabhiṣṭhāḥ*, *raṃhāḥ*, *raṇāḥ*, *rarīthāḥ*, *rejamānāḥ*, *rakṣamāṇāḥ*, *surukmāḥ*, *śucantaḥ*, *avidyuttvāḥ*, *asurathāḥ*, *pitorasāḥ*, *svāninaḥ*, *rudriyāḥ*, *devo rocamānāḥ*, *ṛtoraṇvāḥ*, *rudrā na varti yuvante*, *pūrvaḥ*, *ekayāḥ*, *sarūpāḥ*, *sthātuḥ*, *ghṛtasya*, *divaḥ*, and the last [verse].
(27) The Lokā hymn consists of one verse. (28)

Clothed in splendor, the flickering sparks; being spoken as branches, they grow in the radiant one. The leather straps, the strengths, the offshoots, the enclosures, the most excellent ones; the scattered, the hosts, the longing ones, the speech of all, the garments, the barren cows, the wolves with a hundredfold paths. Like those choosing in the wind, like inspired poets, may they not be separated. Not being of equal mind, they win; we have made them foremost through our finding. They move within like heroes among the clans; the former ones lowing, not surpassed, like a wide expanse in its breadth, beyond the choice, the invoking priests striving, beyond the enclosure.

The gate is beyond the Vedas, not easily reached from before; the great one is beyond the winding paths, the destroyer is beyond those who deceive. When you conquered the adversaries, the contending thoughts and prayers bowed down in submission. Indra, the ancient one, is beyond all—this is the twenty-ninth hymn, consisting of thirty-four verses.

The breaths, most powerful, the glories, the adorned, the helmets, the flames, the supports, the strengtheners, the resting ones, the most beautiful, the spear-like, the oaths, the most loosening; the Soma-drops, your bright ones, grasp what is spread out—the dark ones, praised by the seers, three hundred, well-praised, the wave, the peaceful, the heroes, most bountiful like us, the auspicious ones, the bright ones, come hither; all together, twenty-three. 30.

The *saudhanvana* hymns, the *senā*, the *stokā*, the *siṃha*, the *snā*, the *sarga*, the well-sharpened *soma*, the *svā*, the *stoma*, the pressed *suvāna*, the *svana*, the settled *niṣatta*, the flowing *sasra*, the *sūryāya*, the *sūbharva*, the *surāya*, the *prasunṛta*, the *nara*, the *praspandra*, the *nabhi*, and the *sthira*—may all these be for you, O sinless one. Our thought (*manīṣā*) is desirable, sent forth, directed toward the gods, established in the dwelling-place (*gharmye*), ancient, united, worthy of praise, and true. They have fought; the ancient ones were pressed and praised together. These are the immovable within, while those are the movable; there are thirty-three. 31.

Himā, havamānā, hūyamānā, hinvānā, haryā, huvānā, hvṛtā, hāyā, hetyā, vīrahavyāśca, hā, dīyadraśmāno, hiraṇyayā, vihotrā, hitā, aniṅgyānto, vṛṣṇo, namasā, vātāparjanyāparo, hastāḥ—fifteen [words], 32.
Thus ends the *Śamānaśikṣāmūla*.
